concepts.learning_objective: Explain equality as a moral and political ideal based on the equal worth of all human beings.
Describe the paradox that equality is widely accepted as an ideal while inequality is visible everywhere.

topics.title: What is equality? Equal opportunities and natural versus social inequalities

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why equality means equal access to basic goods and opportunities rather than identical outcomes.
Distinguish natural inequalities from socially-produced inequalities and recognise the limits of this distinction.
Identify the rights that make up political equality and explain why it is necessary but not sufficient.
Explain how social equality requires minimum conditions of life and the removal of discriminatory customs.
Explain the feminist critique of patriarchy and the distinction between sex and gender.

topics.title: Economic equality: Marxism, liberalism and socialism

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how economic inequality is measured and why entrenched inequalities are dangerous.
Compare the Marxist and liberal views on the causes of and remedies for inequality.
Describe the socialist approach to equality and Lohia's idea of Sapta Kranti.

topics.title: Formal equality and equality through differential treatment

concepts.learning_objective: Explain formal equality as the ending of legally protected privileges and discrimination.
Evaluate when differential treatment enhances rather than violates equality.

topics.title: Affirmative action and the debate on reservations

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the rationale and forms of affirmative action and its time-bound nature.
Analyse the arguments of supporters and critics of reservations as policies for equality.
